text: It was Pauls afternoon. <break time="0.8s" /> To appear before the faculty. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the Pittsburgh High School. <break time="0.8s" /> To account for his various misdemeanors. <break time="0.8s" /> For he had been suspended a week before. <break time="0.8s" /> He entered the room smiling. <break time="0.8s" /> And although his clothes were a trifle outgrown. <break time="0.8s" /> There was something of the dandy about him. <break time="0.8s" /> For he wore a red carnation. <break time="0.8s" /> In his buttonhole. <break time="0.8s" /> The faculty felt. <break time="0.8s" /> That this red flower was not at all suited. <break time="0.8s" /> To the contrite spirit. <break time="0.8s" /> That befitted a boy. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had been sent home in disgrace. <break time="0.8s" /> When questioned by the principal. <break time="0.8s" /> Paul stated, politely enough. <break time="0.8s" /> That he wanted to come back to school. <break time="0.8s" /> Though this was a lie. <break time="0.8s" /> For he found lying indispensable. <break time="0.8s" /> For overcoming friction. <break time="0.8s" /> His teachers were asked. <break time="0.8s" /> To state their charges against him. <break time="0.8s" /> Which they did with such rancor and aggrievedness. <break time="0.8s" /> As showed that this was not a usual case. <break time="0.8s" /> Disorder and impertinence. <break time="0.8s" /> Were among the offenses named. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet each instructor felt. <break time="0.8s" /> That the real cause of the trouble. <break time="0.8s" /> Lay in the boys hysterically defiant manner. <break time="0.8s" /> And his open contempt. <break time="0.8s" /> Paul stood through it all smiling. <break time="0.8s" /> His pale lips parted. <break time="0.8s" /> Over his white teeth. <break time="0.8s" /> And he used his eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> In a conscious, theatrical way. <break time="0.8s" /> Peculiarly offensive in a boy. <break time="0.8s" /> Afterward the drawing master. <break time="0.8s" /> Voiced the feeling of them all. <break time="0.8s" /> When he declared. <break time="0.8s" /> That there was something wrong about the fellow. <break time="0.8s" /> Something that none of them understood. <break time="0.8s" /> He had once seen Paul asleep. <break time="0.8s" /> At his desk. <break time="0.8s" /> And he remembered with a shock. <break time="0.8s" /> How old and tired. <break time="0.8s" /> The boys white face had looked. <break time="0.8s" /> As if something were haunting him.
